2. **h02** — Delivery executes in `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`; the actual HTTP call is `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`), fed asynchronously via `webhook.PostAsync` and a 128-slot channel drained by 4 workers (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55,184`). SSRF protection is two-layer: (a) `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) — scheme allowlist plus resolved-IP check against reserved CIDRs (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS 169.254.0.0/16, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10 at `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`), applied on webhook create/update (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`); and (b) dial-time re-checking via `safeDialContext` installed as the HTTP transport's `DialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37,59-74`), which defeats DNS rebinding.

16. **r01** — False premise: there is no Redis anywhere (`grep -ri redis` over all Go code, `go.mod`, `go.sum` returns zero hits). The cache is a hand-rolled in-process, `sync.Map`-based in-memory cache with TTL (`store/cache/cache.go:66`). User entries live in a dedicated `userCache` built at `store/store.go:51-53` with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (`store/store.go:41-45`; package default identical at `store/cache/cache.go:59`); `store/user.go` uses plain `Set`, so users get the 10-minute default TTL.
